messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty autopage -> PD#INC-2025-60211 fired: alert=kubelet_not_ready in gpu-pool-us-east (host=gpu-node-eu-12)
pagerduty: Autopage details: sustained NotReady 2m45s, repeat=3, urgency=high; playbook=https://internal.runbooks/redwood/node-failure
sam: acked. i'm oncall. grabbing serial and checking kubelet logs :eyes:
neha: I can help with traffic mitigation. notifying infra to stop scheduling new test jobs to this pool. I see 4 inference pods pending reschedule
sam: serial log excerpt: ```
[ 4578.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31, GPU hang, context info...
[ 4578.123789] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: status=0x00000001
[ 4578.124000] kernel: kubelet[2345]: E0625 12:34:56.789] Failed to sync pod status: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
[ 4578.125000] watchdog: kernel soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 27s
```
ops-bot: Host gpu-node-eu-12 reported kernel oops and NVRM GPU reset. Logged to hardware-tracker hv-9876
kyle: any immediate customer impact? looking at prod metrics: small P95 spike for image-gen endpoints, throughput steady. no 5xxs.
neha: confirmed: 6 pods moved off this node, 2 retried and recovered. latency bump ~200ms on a few request patterns, affected customers: internal-staging jobs and a handful of low-volume tenants. opening a status page note: "Investigating degraded latency for image-gen routes"
sam: cordoning node and draining with minimal disruption: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-eu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-node-eu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30`
ops-bot: node cordoned: gpu-node-eu-12 -> cordon=true
kyle: good. if pods don't become Ready within 2 min we should spin up additional fallback replicas in fallback-inference. I'll start that if needed.
neha: scaling fallback set to +2 replicas as precaution. watching metrics.
sam: serial shows repeated GPU resets, then kernel panic trace referencing nvlink driver: `gpu0: nvlink timeout, resetting` — trying to capture kmsg to /var/log/incident-1751112222.log
ops-bot: kernel dump captured: /var/lib/kdump/1751112222-gpu-node-eu-12.dump
pagerduty: PD note added: "cordoned and drained; kernel oops with GPU reset; customer impact limited to latency increase, no error spikes"
kyle: can you check whether any Dedicated customers on this host had in-flight requests? If yes, notify their account owners.
neha: looked up tenant mapping: none of the enterprise Dedicated nodes were on gpu-node-eu-12. mainly shared-hosting customers. emailing account owners for the affected tenants now.
sam: attempting soft-reboot via IPMI to preserve logs, will avoid full powercycle unless necessary
ops-bot: IPMI: power-cycle requested by sam -> job 99834
ops-bot: IPMI: host responded to power-cycle and is booting; monitoring boot logs
sam: host booted into rescue image successfully. running vendor SMART and GPU diagnostics: `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0` and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature,utilization --format=csv`
ops-bot: vendor diag returned: nvme SMART shows increased media and read error counts; GPU diagnostics show ECC resets but no persistent fault
kyle: based on diag, I'd lean toward failing NVMe preceded by GPU driver interaction — could be correlated events. recommend RMA for NVMe and schedule host for replacement maintenance window.
neha: created RMA ticket with vendor: RMA-3019, attached kdump and serial logs. Inventory updated: host marked quarantine=true.
sam: adding incident artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1751112222/ (kdump, serial, diag-output, pod-schedule-log). saving path in PD note.
pagerduty: Incident INC-2025-60211 updated: status=identified -> assignee=sam
kyle: I'll stay on the incident for orchestration. @eng-sre I'm going to open a follow-up to evaluate our nvme-health alert thresholds — we only alerted on NotReady, too late here.
neha: action items added to PD: - make nvme SMART warning alert fire earlier - run periodic vendor diagnostics on GPU nodes - add a runbook step to proactively scale fallback pools on GPU host failures
sam: handing off live ops to kyle — I've uploaded all logs and will continue with hardware team asynchronously.
kyle: acknowledged handoff. I'll coordinate scheduling RMA, update status page when maintenance date is set, and drive postmortem. leaving on-call watch for 30m while RMA ticket processes.
ops-bot: PD: set status=monitoring; incident in monitoring for 30m
neha: quick note for customers: status page updated with mitigations and ETA for hardware replacement will be posted when vendor confirms RMA slot
kyle: final operational notes: root cause suspected NVMe degradation causing I/O stalls that triggered GPU resets and kubelet timeouts; mitigation: cordon+drain, scale fallback, RMA NVMe, add proactive SMART alerts.
sam: thanks team, handing off fully. signing out from oncall. :raised_hands:
incident-bot: please open a postmortem PR under /incidents with links to s3://redwood-incidents/1751112222/ and attach kdump. Incident thread archived for live coordination."
